proof:
Source and role. This is step 2 ("Smooth estimate") of the supplied proof of the parent theorem w12_ball_boundary_layer_estimate: a trace-type estimate obtained by integrating along rays from the origin (in textbook proofs of Rellich-Kondrachov the same boundary control comes from an extension operator; Evans 5.7, Gilbarg-Trudinger 7.10). The parent applies it to the smooth approximants supplied by the sibling w12_ball_smooth_approximation and then passes to the limit; this child needs no Sobolev theory.

Notation. R^n is Rn n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure `volume`, an additive Haar measure, and finrank R (Rn n) = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). B_rho := ball(0, rho) is the open ball. A := B_s \ B_{rs} = {x : rs <= |x| < s}. For t > 0 and E a subset of R^n, tE := {tx : x in E}. In Lean `t • E` needs `open scoped Pointwise`; equivalently use the preimage (fun y => t⁻¹ • y) ⁻¹' E. All integrals of nonnegative functions are lintegrals with values in [0, infinity]. |v|^2 means ‖v‖ₑ ^ 2. "int_c^d ... dt" is the lintegral over Icc c d for Lebesgue measure on R. grad phi := gradient phi. Since phi is C^1, Dphi = fderiv R phi is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Hence grad phi = (InnerProductSpace.toDual R (Rn n)).symm ∘ Dphi is continuous, and <grad phi(y), v> = Dphi(y) v (inner_gradient_left).

Hypotheses: n >= 1, phi : R^n -> R is C^1, 1/2 <= r < 1, 0 < s <= 1. Put a := sqrt(1 - r). Claim: int_A |phi|^2 <= 2^{n+3} a (int_{B_s} |phi|^2 + int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2).

Proof.

0. Constants. Since 1/2 <= r < 1, we have 0 < 1 - r <= 1/2. Hence 0 < a <= 1/sqrt 2 < 1 and a^2 = 1 - r. Put tau := 1 - a/2. Then 1/2 < tau < 1 and 1 - tau = a/2 > 0. For every t in [tau, 1] we have 1/2 < t <= 1, hence t^{-n} <= 2^n.

1. Dilation formula. For t > 0, every F : R^n -> [0, infinity] (measurability not needed) and every set E of R^n:
int_E F(tx) dx = t^{-n} int_{tE} F(y) dy.
Proof. T(x) := tx is a homeomorphism of R^n, hence a measurable equivalence: (Homeomorph.smul (Units.mk0 t _)).toMeasurableEquiv. Also T^{-1}(tE) = E (smul_mem_smul_set_iff₀). The pushforward of Lebesgue measure under T is t^{-n} times Lebesgue measure. This is Measure.map_addHaar_smul, map (t • ·) volume = ENNReal.ofReal |(t^n)⁻¹| • volume, together with finrank = n. For a measurable embedding, change of variables holds for every function and every set (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map and MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map):
int_{T^{-1}(S)} F(Tx) dx = int_S F d(T_* volume).
With S = tE, Measure.restrict_smul and lintegral_smul_measure give int_E F(tx) dx = t^{-n} int_{tE} F. (This exact route compiles against the pinned Mathlib; see the formalization note.)

2. Pointwise ray inequality. Let x be in R^n with |x| <= 1, and let t be in [tau, 1]. Put u(sigma) := phi(sigma x) for sigma in R. By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt with sigma -> sigma • x), u is C^1 with u'(sigma) = Dphi(sigma x) x = <grad phi(sigma x), x>, and u' is continuous. By the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt):
phi(x) - phi(tx) = int_t^1 <grad phi(sigma x), x> dsigma (an interval integral).
By Cauchy-Schwarz in R^n and |x| <= 1, |<grad phi(sigma x), x>| <= |grad phi(sigma x)|. With intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_integral_norm, and since [t, 1] is contained in [tau, 1] and the integrand is nonnegative,
|phi(x) - phi(tx)| <= int_t^1 |grad phi(sigma x)| dsigma <= int_tau^1 |grad phi(sigma x)| dsigma.
Bridge between real and extended integrals. The integrands here are continuous and nonnegative on compact intervals. So for c in {t, tau} the real integral over [c, 1] is the real value of the lintegral of the extended norm over Ioc c 1 (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal), and Ioc c 1 differs from Icc c 1 by a null set. The real inequalities of this step therefore transfer to lintegrals over Icc tau 1. Alternatively, do all of step 2 in real numbers and convert once with ENNReal.ofReal; every quantity is finite because phi and grad phi are continuous.
By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on [tau, 1], an interval of length 1 - tau (for instance ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq with p = q = 2 and one factor 1),
(int_tau^1 |grad phi(sigma x)| dsigma)^2 <= (1 - tau) int_tau^1 |grad phi(sigma x)|^2 dsigma.
Finally (p + q)^2 <= 2p^2 + 2q^2 with p = phi(tx) and q = phi(x) - phi(tx). Therefore
(2.1) |phi(x)|^2 <= 2 |phi(tx)|^2 + 2 (1 - tau) G(x),  where G(x) := int_tau^1 |grad phi(sigma x)|^2 dsigma.
Integrate (2.1) over t in [tau, 1], a set of Lebesgue measure 1 - tau. The left side and the last term do not depend on t, so
(2.2) (1 - tau) |phi(x)|^2 <= 2 int_tau^1 |phi(tx)|^2 dt + 2 (1 - tau)^2 G(x).

3. Integration over A and Tonelli. Every x in A satisfies |x| < s <= 1, so (2.2) holds for all x in A. The maps (x, t) -> |phi(tx)|^2 and (x, sigma) -> |grad phi(sigma x)|^2 are continuous on R^n x R, hence measurable. So x -> int_tau^1 |phi(tx)|^2 dt is measurable (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'), and the lintegral of the sum splits (lintegral_add_left). Integrating (2.2) over A, pulling out constants (lintegral_const_mul), and swapping the order of integration (Tonelli, lintegral_lintegral_swap; all measures are s-finite) gives
(3.1) (1 - tau) int_A |phi|^2 <= 2 int_tau^1 I(t) dt + 2 (1 - tau)^2 int_tau^1 J(sigma) dsigma,
where I(t) := int_A |phi(tx)|^2 dx and J(sigma) := int_A |grad phi(sigma x)|^2 dx.

4. Gradient term. Fix sigma in [tau, 1]. By step 1 with F = |grad phi|^2, J(sigma) = sigma^{-n} int_{sigma A} |grad phi|^2. If y = sigma x with x in A, then |y| = sigma |x| < sigma s <= s. So sigma A is contained in B_s, and by step 0,
J(sigma) <= sigma^{-n} int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2 <= 2^n int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2.
Integrating over [tau, 1]: int_tau^1 J(sigma) dsigma <= (1 - tau) 2^n int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2. Hence the second term of (3.1) is at most 2^{n+1} (1 - tau)^3 int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2.

5. Function term and kernel bound. Fix t in [tau, 1]. Since t > 0, y lies in tA iff y/t lies in A iff rst <= |y| < st. By step 1 with F = |phi|^2,
I(t) = t^{-n} int_{tA} |phi|^2 = int_{R^n} |phi(y)|^2 t^{-n} 1[rst <= |y| < st] dy.
The set {(y, t) : rst <= |y| < st} is Borel in R^n x R. So (y, t) -> |phi(y)|^2 t^{-n} 1[rst <= |y| < st] is measurable on R^n x [tau, 1], and Tonelli gives
int_tau^1 I(t) dt = int_{R^n} |phi(y)|^2 k(y) dy,  where k(y) := int_tau^1 t^{-n} 1[rst <= |y| < st] dt.
Kernel bound: k(y) <= 2^{n+1} (1 - r) 1_{B_s}(y) for every y.
(a) If |y| >= s: for t <= 1 we have st <= s <= |y|, so the indicator vanishes on [tau, 1] and k(y) = 0.
(b) If |y| < s: on [tau, 1], t^{-n} <= 2^n by step 0. The indicator is supported where |y|/s < t <= |y|/(rs), because st > |y| and rst <= |y|. This interval has length |y| (1/r - 1)/s <= 1/r - 1 = (1 - r)/r <= 2 (1 - r), using |y| < s and r >= 1/2. Hence k(y) <= 2^n * 2 (1 - r) = 2^{n+1} (1 - r). In lintegral form: k(y) <= 2^n * volume(Ioc (|y|/s) (|y|/(rs))) = 2^n * ENNReal.ofReal (|y|/(rs) - |y|/s) (Real.volume_Ioc). For y = 0 this interval is empty (no t > 0 satisfies rst <= 0), so k(0) = 0.
Therefore int_tau^1 I(t) dt <= 2^{n+1} (1 - r) int_{B_s} |phi|^2, and the first term of (3.1) is at most 2^{n+2} (1 - r) int_{B_s} |phi|^2.

6. Conclusion. Combining (3.1) with steps 4 and 5,
(1 - tau) int_A |phi|^2 <= 2^{n+2} (1 - r) int_{B_s} |phi|^2 + 2^{n+1} (1 - tau)^3 int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2.
Multiply both sides by 2/a = 1/(1 - tau), which is finite and positive (in [0, infinity], ENNReal.ofReal (2/a) * ENNReal.ofReal (1 - tau) = 1). Using 1 - tau = a/2 and 1 - r = a^2:
int_A |phi|^2 <= (2/a) 2^{n+2} a^2 int_{B_s} |phi|^2 + 2^{n+1} (a/2)^2 int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2 = 2^{n+3} a int_{B_s} |phi|^2 + 2^{n-1} a^2 int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2.
Since 0 < a <= 1, 2^{n-1} a^2 <= 2^{n+3} a. Hence
int_A |phi|^2 <= 2^{n+3} a (int_{B_s} |phi|^2 + int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2).
In Lean this is exactly ∫⁻ x in ball 0 s \ ball 0 (r * s), ‖φ x‖ₑ ^ 2 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 ^ (n + 3) * Real.sqrt (1 - r)) * ((∫⁻ x in ball 0 s, ‖φ x‖ₑ ^ 2) + ∫⁻ x in ball 0 s, ‖gradient φ x‖ₑ ^ 2). QED

Formalization note. During decomposition the following proof of the step-1 dilation formula compiled against the pinned Mathlib (lake env lean, in namespace GMT.Ch05.Submission after `import GMT.Ch05.Submission`, with `open scoped Pointwise` added). It may be reused as a helper lemma (rename it, e.g. drop `check`, or make it private, to avoid clashes):

theorem ble_check_lintegral_comp_smul (n : ℕ) (F : Rn n → ℝ≥0∞) (E : Set (Rn n)) (t : ℝ)
    (ht : 0 < t) :
    ∫⁻ x in E, F (t • x) = ENNReal.ofReal ((t ^ n)⁻¹) * ∫⁻ y in t • E, F y := by
  let e : Rn n ≃ᵐ Rn n := (Homeomorph.smul (Units.mk0 t ht.ne')).toMeasurableEquiv
  have he : ∀ x, e x = t • x := fun x => rfl
  have hpre : e ⁻¹' (t • E) = E := by
    ext x
    simp only [mem_preimage, he]
    exact smul_mem_smul_set_iff₀ ht.ne' _ _
  have hmap : Measure.map e volume = ENNReal.ofReal ((t ^ n)⁻¹) • (volume : Measure (Rn n)) := by
    have := Measure.map_addHaar_smul (volume : Measure (Rn n)) ht.ne'
    rw [finrank_euclideanSpace_fin] at this
    rw [show (e : Rn n → Rn n) = fun x => t • x from funext he, this]
    congr 2
    rw [abs_of_pos (by positivity)]
  calc ∫⁻ x in E, F (t • x) = ∫⁻ x in e ⁻¹' (t • E), F (e x) := by rw [hpre]; simp only [he]
    _ = ∫⁻ y in t • E, F y ∂(Measure.map e volume) := by
        rw [e.measurableEmbedding.restrict_map, e.measurableEmbedding.lintegral_map]
    _ = _ := by rw [hmap, Measure.restrict_smul, lintegral_smul_measure, smul_eq_mul]
key_steps: Constants: a = sqrt(1-r) in (0, 1/sqrt 2], a^2 = 1-r, tau = 1 - a/2 in (1/2, 1), 1 - tau = a/2, and t^{-n} <= 2^n on [tau, 1]
Dilation formula int_E F(tx) dx = t^{-n} int_{tE} F for t > 0 (map_addHaar_smul plus a measurable equivalence)
Ray FTC and Cauchy-Schwarz: (1-tau)|phi(x)|^2 <= 2 int_tau^1 |phi(tx)|^2 dt + 2(1-tau)^2 int_tau^1 |grad phi(sigma x)|^2 dsigma for |x| <= 1
Integrate over A = B_s minus B_{rs} and swap the order of integration by Tonelli
Gradient term: sigma A lies in B_s, giving at most 2^{n+1}(1-tau)^3 int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2
Function term: the kernel int_tau^1 t^{-n} 1[rst <= |y| < st] dt is at most 2^{n+1}(1-r) 1_{B_s}(y), giving at most 2^{n+2}(1-r) int_{B_s} |phi|^2
Divide by 1 - tau = a/2 and use a <= 1 to obtain the constant 2^{n+3} a
